question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, with MRI (FreeSurfer regional measures) as the shared channel. P-211 (Cai et al., Brain Sci 2023) uses an Explainable Boosting Machine on baseline MRI volumes/thickness plus cognitive scores, demographics and APOE4, at horizons of 1-5 years. P-179 (Li et al., Brain Sci 2021) uses sMRI ROI volumes plus peripheral-blood SNP genotypes and mRNA expression, with molecular subtyping and a multiple-kernel classifier, for conversion within 3 years. Added channels (cognitive tests vs blood omics), horizon and sample differ, which condition 1 allows.

figures.P-211: Five-year horizon, Comb (a): AUC 0.92 (225 participants: 140 MCI/85 dementia), no interval printed. Hanley-McNeil over the 5-fold CV sample: Q1 = 0.8519, Q2 = 0.8817, SE = 0.0214, CI [0.878, 0.962]; over a 10% test set (about 9/14): CI [0.788, 1.000]. Three-year horizon, test data: AUC 0.81 with interactions (0.78 without); 3-year cohort 392 MCI/188 dementia. Over a 10% test set (about 19/39): SE 0.0659, CI [0.681, 0.939]; over the whole 3-year cohort: SE 0.0207, CI [0.769, 0.851].
figures.P-179: Internal 5-fold CV in ADNI-1 (125 MCI): AUC 0.826 (MCI-CPS); no-subtyping classifier 0.785. External ADNI-GO/2 test (98 MCI): AUC 0.781. No AUC intervals printed. Class sizes from the printed sensitivity/specificity: internal 81.25% = 39/48 and 77.92% = 60/77, so 48 pMCI/77 sMCI (99/125 = 79.20% accuracy); external 74.19% = 23/31 and 74.63% = 50/67, so 31/67 (73/98 = 74.49%). Hanley-McNeil, internal: Q1 = 0.826/1.174 = 0.7036, Q2 = 2(0.826^2)/1.826 = 0.7473, SE = 0.0406, CI [0.746, 0.906]. External: SE 0.0539, CI [0.675, 0.887].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. P-211 reports its result at P-179's three-year horizon: AUC 0.81 (0.78 without interaction effects). 0.81 lies inside both P-179 intervals (internal [0.746, 0.906], external [0.675, 0.887]). P-179's 0.826 and 0.781 both lie inside P-211's three-year interval at either evaluation-set n ([0.681, 0.939]; [0.769, 0.851]). The matched figures agree in both directions. The headline pair (0.92 five-year vs 0.826 three-year) is apart beyond uncertainty in both directions if the 0.92 is taken over the 225-participant CV sample (0.92 above P-179's 0.906; 0.826 below 0.878), but that gap is P-211's five-year horizon.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 0.92 and 0.826 are below 0.97.
reason: The recorded gap sets P-211's five-year AUC (0.92) against P-179's three-year AUC (0.83). At the matched three-year horizon P-211 prints 0.81, which agrees in both directions with P-179's internal 0.826 and external 0.781. The papers' own figures dissolve the gap, so condition 3 fails.

quotes.quote: The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.
All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.
